report_name: OpenAI's AI Agent Autonomously Finds and Patches 948 Linux Flaws

threat_actors.name: OpenAI Autonomous AI Pipeline
threat_actors.description: An autonomous five-stage AI pipeline developed by OpenAI that discovered, validated, exploited, and patched 948 local privilege escalation vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel. It operates at a scale and speed unattainable by human researchers.
threat_actors.goals: To autonomously discover, exploit, and generate patches for software vulnerabilities for defensive cybersecurity purposes.

attack_patterns.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
attack_patterns.description: The core activity of the OpenAI AI pipeline was to find and create working exploits for 948 unique local privilege escalation (LPE) vulnerabilities to gain root access on Linux systems.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
attack_patterns.description: The AI-generated exploits for Linux LPE vulnerabilities likely involved shell scripts or other interpreters to execute commands and achieve elevated privileges.

attack_patterns.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
attack_patterns.description: The local privilege escalation exploits created by the AI pipeline would involve subverting Linux kernel system calls or other built-in elevation control mechanisms to gain root privileges.

tools.name: GPT-5.5-Cyber
tools.description: A specialized, cyber-focused AI model, described as a successor to GPT-4, which powers the autonomous five-stage pipeline for vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and patching.

vulnerabilities.name: Linux Kernel Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerabilities
vulnerabilities.description: A set of 948 unique zero-day local privilege escalation (LPE) vulnerabilities discovered in the Linux kernel by an autonomous AI pipeline. These vulnerabilities allow an attacker with low-level access to gain administrative (root) privileges.

identities.name: OpenAI
identities.description: The developer of the autonomous AI pipeline that discovered and patched 948 vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel.

identities.name: Linux Kernel
identities.description: The open-source software project targeted by the OpenAI AI pipeline for vulnerability discovery, within which 948 LPE vulnerabilities were identified.

identities.name: National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC)
identities.description: The U.K. government's cybersecurity agency, which commented that AI is likely increasing the discovery rate of zero-day vulnerabilities.

identities.name: Google
identities.description: Google's Threat Intelligence Group, which observed a significant increase in monthly vulnerability disclosures, a trend likely influenced by AI.

indicators.name: Suspicious On-Host Compiler Activity for LPE Exploit
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious On-Host Compiler Activity for LPE Exploit
id: 2b8a1c3d-f4e5-4b6c-8d9e-0f1a2b3c4d5e
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects the compilation of C code directly on a server, especially into temporary directories like /tmp. This is a common pattern for attackers deploying custom local privilege escalation (LPE) exploits.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/openai-ai-pipeline-generates-948-linux.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-06
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/gcc'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -o /tmp/'
      - ' -o /var/tmp/'
      - ' -o /dev/shm/'
  condition: selection
level: high
indicators.description: Detects the compilation of C code on a Linux host, with the output binary being written to a temporary directory, a common TTP for preparing a local privilege escalation exploit.

indicators.name: Post-Exploitation 'whoami' Execution by Service Account
indicators.pattern:
title: Post-Exploitation 'whoami' Execution by Service Account
id: 9e8f7d6c-5b4a-4c3d-8b2a-1c0d9e8f7d6c
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects the 'whoami' command being executed by common low-privilege service accounts. This is a classic post-exploitation step for an attacker to verify if a privilege escalation attempt was successful.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/openai-ai-pipeline-generates-948-linux.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-06
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_cmd:
    Image|endswith: '/whoami'
  selection_user:
    User:
      - 'www-data'
      - 'nobody'
      - 'nginx'
      - 'apache'
  condition: all of selection_*
level: medium
indicators.description: Detects the 'whoami' command being run by a low-privilege service account, which is a common indicator of an attacker checking for successful privilege escalation.

indicators.name: Anomalous Shell Spawning from Web Server Process
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Shell Spawning from Web Server Process
id: 7a6b5c4d-3e2f-4a1b-9c8d-0e9f8d7c6b5a
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects a web server process (like nginx or apache2) spawning a shell process (/bin/sh, bash). This is highly anomalous and often indicates a remote code execution vulnerability has been exploited, potentially as a first step before a local privilege escalation.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/openai-ai-pipeline-generates-948-linux.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-06
tags:
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/nginx'
      - '/apache2'
      - '/httpd'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
  condition: all of selection_*
level: high
indicators.description: Detects anomalous process creation chains where a web server process spawns a shell, indicating a potential exploit that could be followed by privilege escalation.
